newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares up slightly on support, volume fall.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares up slightly on support, volume fall.

text.p: Istanbul shares edged higher on Wednesday on technical support which emerged at the index's 1,550 level, but volume dived amid political concerns and the absence of moving expectations, brokers said.

The IMKB National-100 closed at 1,582, up five points, or 0.32 percent from Tuesday when it plunged 4.48 percent on renewed political worries ahead of a National Security Council (MGK) meeting expected next week.
Trade volume further shrank to 19.75 trillion lira from Tuesday's 26.15 trillion and Monday's 40.73 trillion lira.

"Both the trade range and volume were narrow because of the market's inspired state. Signs that political tension may again mount is affecting the market which may drift sideways with selective activity until the MGK meeting," said Ibrahim Basnur from Ar securities.

The coalition government's Islamist wing opposes a plan to raise compulsory education to eight years from five as part of measures put forward at the military-dominated MGK's February 28 meeting to clamp down on rising Islamist activism.

The proposal almost completed by the education ministry has drawn protest from supporters of Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan's Islamist Welfare Party, who fear it will spell the end of religious schools.

Of the 238 issues traded, falls outdid rises by 111 to 57 and 70 closed steady. The IMKB Industrial firmed 0.88 percent to 1,600, the IMKB Services edged up 0.41 percent to 1,471 while the IMKB Financial eased 0.3 percent to 1,672.
Top actives were T.Isbank's C series, up 500 lira at 46,000 and state-run Turkish Airlines, up 2,500 lira at 39,500. They made up 13.5 percent of the total turnover.
